references.text: In [ref:Joh 20:3-10|John 20:3-10], the parallel account is told of how Peter (along with the other disciple) ran to the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there. This is the most detailed parallel to Luke's description of Peter's visit to the empty tomb.
[ref:Joh 20:6-7|John 20:6-7] specifically describes how Peter entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths (ὀθόνια) lying there, using the same Greek word as in Luke 24:12.

In [ref:Luk 24:24|Luke 24:24], the travelers to Emmaus refer back to this visit: "Some of those who were with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him." This confirms Peter's visit to the tomb.
[ref:Luk 24:1-9|Luke 24:1-9] is the immediate context: the women's visit to the empty tomb and their report to the disciples, which prompted Peter to run there.
[ref:Luk 24:10-11|Luke 24:10-11] tells that the disciples did not believe the women's message – this is what motivated Peter to get up and run to the tomb to see for himself.
[ref:Mark 16:1-8|Mark 16:1-8] is Mark's account of the empty tomb, which forms the background for Peter's visit.

[ref:Joh 19:40|John 19:40] tells that Jesus' body was wrapped in linen cloths (ὀθόνια) with fragrant spices according to Jewish burial custom. It was precisely these linen cloths that Peter found lying alone in the tomb.
[ref:Luk 23:53|Luke 23:53] describes how Joseph of Arimathea took Jesus' body down, wrapped it in linen (σινδόν), and laid it in the tomb. Peter now only found the linen cloths left behind.
